points.t: Tingling, then **grouped vesicles** and crust at the **same spot** on the lip, recurring with triggers.
HSV-1 latent in the **trigeminal ganglion** reactivates and travels down the nerve.
Topical aciclovir at the first tingle, SPF lip balm, no kissing; oral antivirals if severe or frequent.
Eczema herpeticum, herpetic eye disease, neonates, chronic ulcers in immunosuppression.

cause.lead: A virus that sleeps in a nerve and wakes with triggers.
points: Spread by contact with lesions or **asymptomatic shedding** (saliva).
After primary infection (often childhood gingivostomatitis) it stays **latent in the trigeminal ganglion**.
**Triggers**: fever, URTI, UV, cold wind, menstruation, stress, dental or lip procedures.
Recurs at the **same site**; immunosuppression → larger, chronic ulcers.

visuals.caption: Latency and reactivation: the virus rests in the trigeminal ganglion in front of the ear, then travels down the sensory nerve to the same spot on the lip each time.
visuals.alt: Head diagram showing HSV in the trigeminal ganglion travelling to the lip

features.lead: Tingle → blisters → ulcer → crust in 7–10 days.
points: **Grouped small vesicles** on a red base at the vermilion border.
→ pustules → painful erosions → crust → heals in **7–10 days**, no scar.
A few recurrences a year is typical; > 6 a year in some.
Other HSV: cheek, **whitlow**, gladiatorum, **eczema herpeticum**, keratitis, HSV-associated EM.

visuals.caption: The stages of a cold sore at the lip border: redness and tingling, grouped clear vesicles, burst weeping erosions, then a dry golden-brown crust.
visuals.alt: Four stages of a cold sore on the lip

points: **HSV PCR** if atypical, severe, immunocompromised, near the eye, or recurrent EM.
Eczema, pregnancy near term, neonates nearby, immunosuppression?

cards.name: Impetigo
cards.clue: Honey crusts, spreading, children; no prodrome.

cards.name: Herpes zoster
cards.clue: Dermatomal, more painful, usually one episode.

cards.name: Angular cheilitis
cards.clue: Fissured mouth corners; dentures, iron / B12.

cards.name: Fixed drug eruption
cards.clue: Same site with each dose; dusky patch.

cards.name: EM / SJS
cards.clue: Targets, several mucosae, drug history: urgent if extensive.

manage.lead: Based on NICE CKS Herpes simplex – oral.

points: Paracetamol or ibuprofen; fluids; cold-sore patches for comfort.
Don’t pick; wash hands; no sharing cups or lip products.
**Avoid kissing** (especially neonates, eczema, immunosuppressed); **SPF 30+** lip balm.

rx.note: Modest benefit (~½–1 day shorter). Penciclovir 1% alternative.
UK SmPC cold-sore regimen; check formulary.
Frequent / severe recurrences or HSV-associated EM; specialist advice often sought.

points: Higher dose / longer oral antivirals; **specialist advice**; IV for chronic large ulcers.

limits.t: Benefit falls sharply once vesicles form.

items.t: Punched-out erosions spreading over eczema: **eczema herpeticum**.
Red painful eye, photophobia, blurred vision, vesicles on nose tip: **ophthalmology**. Never topical steroid.
**Neonate** (< 1 month) or primary HSV late in pregnancy.
Immunosuppressed with extensive or non-healing lesions (> 2 weeks).
Child with gingivostomatitis not drinking, or recurrent erythema multiforme.

pearls.t: Same place + recurrent = HSV; one-off band of vesicles = zoster.
Frequent severe recurrences: consider immunosuppression (e.g. HIV testing if risk).
Aciclovir: reduce dose in renal impairment; keep hydrated.

quiz.a: 5% cream five times daily for 5 days, started at the first tingle.

quiz.q: An oral option for a severe cold sore in an adult?
quiz.a: Aciclovir 400 mg five times daily for 5 days, or valaciclovir 2 g twice daily for 1 day.

quiz.q: Vesicles on the nose tip with a red painful eye?
quiz.a: Possible herpetic eye disease: same-day ophthalmology; no topical steroid.
